title: Sticky KV offsets & attention-mode probe — scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent inference stalls / repeated token omission observed when handling very long prefixes (>12k tokens) with mixed short/long request traffic. Issue surfaced on Dedicated cluster g4-2 (L) after we rolled kernel-selection heuristics change (PR 482).
- Symptoms: single requests hang for multiple seconds between tokens, KV offsets in traces jump (offset drift), and attention mode toggles (dense->sparse heuristics) mid-request leading to kernel-mismatch errors.

Observed during incidents (summary):
- 2025-11-12: first noisy report from canary: latency spikes for a multi-turn chat session.
- 2025-12-03: reproduction on staging with long prefix (14k tokens): saw token drop + 500-level internal errors in runtime logs.
- 2026-01-29: spike after enabling dynamic attention-mode fallback in routing policy.

Quick reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Start local runtime binary with --trace-kv --trace-attn-mode --hotpatch-kernel-selection off
2) Send a coupled workload: 80% short prompt (<=64), 20% long-context stream (13k prefix + 512 generation).
3) Observe runtime logs and /metrics endpoint.

Commands I ran (notes and outputs inline):
- Start runtime (deterministic seed):
  ./run-runtime --model rwd-7b --gpus 1 --trace-kv --trace-attn-mode 
  (used image: rwd/runtime:2025-11-01-canary)

- Reproduce client load:
  python tools/load_gen.py --concurrency 4 --ratio 0.8:0.2 --short-len 32 --long-prefix-file tests/14k-prefix.txt --gen-len 512

- Capture logs to trace file:
  sudo journalctl -u runtime.service -f > /tmp/runtime.trace.log &

Snippets from /tmp/runtime.trace.log (abridged):
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.312Z [kv] alloc-offset id=0x7fb1e4b0 drift_delta=4096 -> 8192
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.313Z [attn] select-kernel: heuristic=seq_len_based, chosen=opt_dense_v2, fallback=opt_sparse_v1
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.314Z [runtime] warning: kv-offset-mismatch detected for req=0x9f3a, expected-offset=2147483648, observed-offset=2147487744
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.316Z [rpc] send-token error: code=E_INTERNAL, msg="kv-index-out-of-sync"

Additional diagnostic capture (traces/kv-index.csv):
- columns: timestamp, req_id, kv_layer, offset_expected, offset_observed, seq_len, attn_mode
- sample line: 2026-01-29T14:22:41.312Z,0x9f3a,kv1,2147483648,2147487744,13122,dense

My immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Offset wrap/overflow handling bug when prefix lengths approach 2^31-ish boundary in signed offsets representation — observed large base numbers in logs.
2) Kernel-selection race: heuristic toggles (dense->sparse) while a request is mid-flight, code path expects a consistent kernel and KV index layout and fails when kernels with different KV packing are switched.
3) Eviction/compaction race: background compaction moves KV slots and updates global base offset while in-flight requests still reference old offsets.
4) Mis-encoded pointer arithmetic in the runtime layer when handling concatenated prefix + generation, producing 4k-aligned jumps (I see multiples of 4096 in drift logs).

Experiments already tried (results):
- Force single kernel via env: RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=opt_dense_v2 -> reproduced but less frequently; still saw offset drift on very long prefixes. (implication: not only kernel switching)
- Disable background compaction: set KV_COMPACT_INTERVAL=0 -> reproduction rate dropped significantly, suggests compaction involvement.
- Increase KV lock granularity (coarse lock across layers): eliminated the offset mismatch in short test but caused latency regressions for high concurrency.
- Run with unsigned offsets patch (local build): removed negative values but drift still occurs when base offset crosses 4k multiples.

Small local patch I tried (do not merge):
- Add extra atomic fence in kv_index_update() right after base_offset increment. Observed temporary reduction in races during synthetic mixed workload.
- Diff snippet: "atomic_thread_fence(memory_order_seq_cst); write(base_offset); atomic_thread_fence(memory_order_seq_cst);"

Logs showing kernel-change mid-request (interesting):
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.310Z [attn] req=0x9f3a seq_prefix=13122 current_choice=opt_dense_v2
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.312Z [metrics] percent_long=0.198 throughput=420
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.313Z [attn] heuristic-updated seq_len_avg=12600 -> select sparse for new inflight batch
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.314Z [kv] req=0x9f3a performing kv_read(offset=2147483648) -> returned index mapped to dense-layout
- 2026-01-29T14:22:41.316Z [attn] error: kernel-layout-mismatch -> E_INTERNAL

Where kernel-selection lives (notes):
- module: runtime/attn/kernel_selector.cc
- exported endpoint for hotpatch: /config/kernel_selector (used by rollout controller)
- selection inputs: seq_len_histogram (sliding window), latency budget, model_family, quantization_profile

Important micro-observation:
- The drift values are almost always multiples of 4096. Hypothesis: page-aligned offsets due to chunk-based allocation.
- The problem reproduces far more on NVMe-backed KV shards than on RAM-only. Disk compaction path likely moves whole chunks.

Short-term mitigations I proposed to SRE on call:
- Revert dynamic attention-mode rollout to last-known-good config (disabled 2026-01-30).
- Increase KV compaction interval on affected dedicated clusters (30min -> 6h).
- Add runtime flag to pin kernel per-request: --pin-kernel-per-request (rollout as emergency toggle).

Next experiments to run (priority order):
- Add a per-request kernel-stability tag: attach chosen_kernel_id to request metadata and refuse kernel hot-switch until request completes. Reproduce.
- Instrument compaction to publish before/after mapping snapshot in S3 for failed requests to correlate observed offsets.
- Add delta-check on kv_read: if observed_offset != expected_offset and abs(delta) % 4096 == 0 -> log additional compaction context.
- Create synthetic compaction-heavy test that moves chunks during live requests to verify race.

Unanswered questions / open threads:
- Why do NVMe shards show worse behavior? Are IO latency jitter and compaction timing coupling into our heuristic window?
- How does quantization profile affect kernel layout? Could different quantized formats change KV packing assumptions?
- Can we change offsets to be stable ids (indirection table) instead of physical offsets to avoid shift problems?

Immediate TODOs for me:
- [ ] Build instrumented runtime with per-request kernel_id + extra KV snapshot logging (target: 2026-02-20)
- [ ] Run compaction stress test on staging and capture traces (target: 2026-02-22)
- [ ] Draft a safe hotfix: enforce kernel pinning during in-flight request (RFC to runtime-prs)
- [ ] Sync with storage team about NVMe compaction knobs and metadata snapshotting

Notes to reviewers / hints if you pick this up:
- Look first at runtime/kv/compactor.{cc,h} and runtime/attn/kernel_selector.cc. The race probably crosses the boundary between those modules.
- Use long-prefix test data (tests/14k-prefix.txt) and the load_gen script above; don't forget to set RUNTIME_TRACE_KV=1.
- Be careful: coarse locks hide race but cause SLO regressions; aim for a correctness-first patch with a path to incremental performance improvements.

End of scratchpad.
